applied.problem: The 362 N m wheel torque is stated as fact though it is the loss-free value, and the same text later gives 344 N m; and "a coupling needs its centre lines in one straight line" is absolute, while universal couplings work at an angle and real alignment is to a tolerance.

Waiting for shafts to stop is not enough on a hoist like the worked example: a hanging load can drive the gears with the motor isolated. And "no angle and no offset" is unachievable as written; shafts are aligned to within a tolerance.
"A real belt creeps" is too general: toothed (synchronous) belts do not creep; creep belongs to flat and V-belts.
